title: CAT 2024 Question Paper (Slot 1, QA) - Quant - Logarithms Exponents
subject: Quant

questions.q: The sum of all real values of ${k}$ for which $(\frac{1}{8})^k \times(\frac{1}{32768})^{\frac{1}{3}}=\frac{1}{8} \times(\frac{1}{32768})^{\frac{1}{k}}$, is
questions.explain: The equation can be written in terms of powers of 2. Since $8=2^3$ and $32768=2^{15}$, the equation is $(2^{-3})^k \times (2^{-15})^{1/3} = 2^{-3} \times (2^{-15})^{1/k}$. This simplifies to $2^{-3k} \times 2^{-5} = 2^{-3} \times 2^{-15/k}$, so $2^{-3k-5} = 2^{-3-15/k}$. Equating exponents gives $-3k-5 = -3-15/k$. Multiplying by ${k}$ yields the quadratic equation $3k^2+2k-15=0$. For a quadratic equation $ax^2+bx+c=0$, the sum of the roots is $-b/a$. Here, the sum of values for ${k}$ is $-2/3$.

questions.q: If ${x}$ is a positive real number such that $4 \log _{10} x+4 \log _{100} x+8 \log _{1000} x=13$, then the greatest integer not exceeding ${x}$, is
questions.explain: Using the change of base formula, $\log_{100} x = (\log_{10} x)/2$ and $\log_{1000} x = (\log_{10} x)/3$. The equation becomes $4\log_{10} x + 4(\frac{\log_{10} x}{2}) + 8(\frac{\log_{10} x}{3}) = 13$. Let $L=\log_{10}x$. Then $4L+2L+(8/3)L=13 \Rightarrow 6L+(8/3)L = 13 \Rightarrow (26/3)L=13 \Rightarrow L=1.5$. So $x=10^{1.5} = 10\sqrt{10} = \sqrt{1000}$. Since $31^2 = 961$ and $32^2 = 1024$, the value of ${x}$ is between 31 and 32. The greatest integer not exceeding ${x}$ is 31.
